newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest power extends gains on cold, natgas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest power extends gains on cold, natgas.

text.p: Wholesale spot electricity prices for the U.S. Midwest were higher again Tuesday, lifted by severely cold weather in the region and significantly stronger natural gas prices, industry sources said.

Temperatures throughout most of the Midwest are expected to be much below normal through at least early next week, with temperatures falling about 20-30 degrees Fahrenheit below normal Wednesday through Friday in the southern plains.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm power prices for Wednesday delivery were steady to higher in the $28.00-31.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, as compared with Monday's range of $28.00-28.50, market sources said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power deals were assessed steady around $13.00-14.00.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Wednesday delivery were higher in the $30.00-32.00 range, up from the $25.00-27.00 range seen on Monday.
MAIN off peak power was notionally assessed in the $14.00-15.00 range, mostly steady from Monday.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Wednesday were higher at $28.00-30.00, with some deals reported done as high as $35.00 as buyers scrambled to meet the plentiful heating demand. These prices compare with Monday's $23.00-26.00 trading range.
"A lot of people are doing hourly trading tomorrow. They're not pre-scheduling," one source said, which caused the volatility in the market.
For the remainder of December, peak ECAR prices were talked in the $28.10-28.40 range.
January/February ECAR prices were in the $25.00-26.00 range, as compared with $25.25-25.50 evident on Monday.
The March market was pegged in the $21.25-22.00 area.
July/August ECAR prices were talked in the $27.00-27.50 range.
Off-peak, non-firm next-day ECAR power hovered at $15.00-16.00.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), peak non-firm power for Wednesday was quoted mostly in the $30.00-32.00 range, as compared with Monday's $25.00-26.00 trading range.
January/February peak prices in SPP were talked about 25 cents higher in the $28.50-29.00 range.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were notionally around $13.00.
Consumers Power's 67 megawatt (MW) Big Rock Point nuclear power unit in Charlevoix, Mich., shut last Friday, will be down for about 30 to 45 days, the company said.
Also, Northern States Power Co's 222 MW Riverside 8 coal unit, in Minneapolis, Minn., has returned to service after shutting Friday.

Contributing to the stronger electricity prices were the higher, but volatile, natural gas prices. In the Midcontinent, gas for Wednesday delivery traded anywhere from $4.50 to about $4.85, with the bulk of the deals done in the low-$4.60s.
((H McCulloch, New York Power Desk +212-859-1628))
